newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat seeding progresses but lags average.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat seeding progresses but lags average.

text.p: Seedbed preparation and planting in Oklahoma wheat fields advanced as drier weather moved in during the week ended Sunday, the state agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.

But progress on wheat seeding still lagged average levels. Wheat was three percent seeded versus 10 last year and the 11 percent average. Only 63 percent of seedbeds were prepared against 73 last year and 80 on average.
Despite the overall dry weather, scattered thunderstorms dropped substantial rain in some areas of the southwest and central districts of Oklahoma.
Corn harvested 10 percent vs 15 year ago, 32 average.
Corn mature 30 percent vs 67 y/a, 80 avge.
Corn rated 92 percent good to excellent, 7 fair, 1 poor.
Sorghum harvested 4 percent vs 1 y/a, 2 avge.
Sorghum mature 24 percent vs 8 y/a, 14 avge.
Sorghum rated 93 pct good to excellent, 5 fair, 2 poor.
Soybeans harvested 6 percent vs 5 y/a, 5 avge.
Soybeans mature 28 pct vs 25 y/a, 23 avge.
Soybeans rated 69 pct good to excellent, 23 fair, 6 poor.
Cotton bolls opening 16 percent vs 4 y/a, 15 avge.
Cotton rated 61 pct good to excellent, 21 fair, 18 poor to very poor.
Pasture and range condition was rated 74 pct good to excellent, versus 83 percent at that level last week.
